subject: [FinServe] Cold-boot latency surge — exec action plan and temporary mitigations
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@finserve.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 17:10:00 -0400
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on our production integration around 23:40 EDT Monday night. 90% of requests are fine but p95 jumped to ~1.6s (baseline ~350ms) and p99 is spiking up to 6–8s. This correlates with autoscaling events — looks like requests hit cold instances during a burst.

We attached traces and a short p99 CSV. This is impacting time-sensitive payment authorization calls; our ops team is seeing errors when the client times out. Please treat as urgent — we need a mitigation and ETA for a fix.

Att: finserve-traces-20280321.zip, p99-report-march21.csv

Thanks,
Marta Gomez
Head of Platform Reliability
FinServe Inc.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@finserve.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 17:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

Marta — thanks for the data and the heads up. Sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating to our engineering and operations leads (cc'd).

Immediate plan: Marcus and Evelyn will triage the traces to confirm whether this is a cold-start initialization path in the GPU autoscaler or a request-routing regression. We will propose a short-term mitigation (minutes-hours) and a follow-up plan with timeline (hours-days). Priya and Aditya are on copy for customer communication and any credit/contract questions.

I'll come back with an ETA within 30 minutes.

— Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 17:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

On Tue, Mar 21, 2028 at 5:25 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marta — thanks for the data and the heads up.

Looking through the traces quickly: the stack shows a long tail inside process startup (~3.8s) on the first token for affected requests — we see GPU driver init + model kernel selection + KV cache cold path. Autoscaler logs show a surge and pool fill events ~23:38–23:41 with ~15 instances spun up within 90s.

Hypothesis: the combination of (1) aggressive batch sizing in dispatcher and (2) lazy per-instance kernel linking leads to per-request stalls on first invocation. This matches a cold-boot class of regression rather than a routing issue.

Immediate asks for Evelyn/ops:
- Push a temporary routing override to prefer warm pool instances for FinServe traffic.
- If warm capacity isn't available, reduce dispatcher max batch size to avoid blocking on kernel init.
- Gather full gc/driver logs for the spun-up instances (I'll attach commands).

I can prepare a hotfix to reduce the lazy-link window and enable prelinking for the most used kernels, but that will take a day to QA.

—Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

On Tue, Mar 21, 2028 at 5:40 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hypothesis: ... lazy per-instance kernel linking leads to per-request stalls on first invocation.

Agree with Marcus. Short-term mitigation (we can apply in the next 15–45 minutes):
- Route FinServe to the warm standby pool in us-east-1 (will add ~3–6s of extra tail capacity but eliminate cold boot on their critical path).
- Enable instance prelinking on the model variant FinServe uses (config toggle we can flip safely; will add ~200MB memory overhead).
- Drop dispatcher max batch size from 64->24 for FinServe to reduce blocking on kernel init.

Medium-term (1–2 days):
- Backport a prelink early-init patch (Marcus) to reduce first-token latency by precompiling kernels during instance bootstrap.
- Add a policy to maintain a small number of pinned warm instances for customers with <1s SLOs during burst windows.

Customer-facing language / credits: we should offer a one-time usage credit and a joint post-mortem. Priya — can you prepare the credit/communications package? Aditya — helpful if you can brief sales leadership.

I'll coordinate the rollout with infra and confirm once routing override is active.

—Evelyn
Director, Production Operations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@finserve.com>
Cc: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 18:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

Marta — update and immediate plan: 

1) We are routing FinServe traffic to our warm standby pool in us-east-1 now (in progress; should be transparent).
2) We toggled instance prelinking for the model variant you're using — this will remove much of the first-token init cost.
3) Dispatcher batch size for your key has been reduced to avoid blocking during kernel init.

Evelyn and Marcus are tracking a medium-term patch that will precompile kernels on bootstrap (ETA 24–48 hours for QA + staged rollout).

We will monitor closely for the next 3 hours and follow up with a post-mortem and recommended config changes. Priya will send proposed account credit for the incident.

Apologies for the impact — we're treating this as high priority and will keep you updated every 2 hours until we confirm stabilization.

— Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@finserve.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finserve.com
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — Monday night batch, Hosted API

Rishi / team — thanks for the quick response and the temporary mitigations. We observe p99 back down to ~700–850ms during the 06:00–08:30 window (compared to 6–8s). That's better and acceptable for now while you roll the patch.

Please proceed with the post-mortem and provide the timeline for the prelink fix. We'll expect the credit proposal from Priya and the follow-up doc with SLO guidance for bursty workloads.

Marta
Head of Platform Reliability
FinServe Inc.
